metadata.Description: This Art Reel features two works inscribed by the artist Kit Stokoe (Kitashi) as part of The Low-Res Derivative Art Collection. Upon inscription, these works were not made children to the parent ordinal of the series, The Low-Res Pear (Ordinal #0), nor were they given any on-chain metadata. For this reason, this ‘Art Reel’ has been inscribed to showcase the works in a way that officially establishes them as part of the Collection. The ‘Art Reel’ Ordinal itself is also a work of art in its own right and a key piece in the Low-Res Derivative Art Series. Show Reels are rare within the Collection, and only two Show Reels serve to establish the existence of some very early Low-Res works, the other show cases Ordinals #3 & #5. There are also other Low-Res Derivative Art Reels that exist outside of a Parent-Child link to the Collection. These Art Reels are equally part of the Low-Res Art Series.

metadata.Original Medium: Acrylic Paint on a 1/4" Acrylic Sheet
metadata.Description: Melissa Ayr’s “Ayr Lungs” collection signals to the World that we need to breathe. Neither coronavirus nor cops can keep us from our creativity and expression. The window is the view we see whilst being trapped in our homes and seen through a screen. The lungs represent the air we need. Our heart is open and ready to receive love in sickness or on the street. 'Breathe' was the first in this collection of 'Ayr Lungs' created in 2020. The piece features a dynamic interplay of vibrant colors, including deep blues, fiery reds, and warm oranges, contrasted by lighter splashes of white and subtle earth tones, all swirling together to evoke the life-giving force of air and the emotional intensity of love.
metadata.Additional_information: The 'Ayr Lungs' collection can be found at https://melissaayr.com/ayr-lungs. The collection is a powerful reminder of the importance of air, creativity, and love in challenging times.

attributes.value: The serenity of an autumn park

metadata.comment 1: I created this image for Twitter, where Ritsu is my avatar. I decided to depict Ritsu walking in the park, holding a bunch of yellow fallen leaves to emphasize that autumn is in full swing. The result turned out to be especially captivating! It perfectly captures the warm, sunny vibes of a beautiful autumn day. I didn’t expect such a wonderful outcome from an AI-based image generator. I hope my followers appreciated the picture as much as I do.
metadata.comment 2: The original JPEG file size was 130,266 bytes. Now, after conversion to the WEBP format, it’s only 71,442 bytes. I reduced the image size to save space on the Bitcoin network (remember, the maximum size for an entire Bitcoin block should not exceed 4 MB). When preparing this image for inscription, I was concerned that inscribing a large amount of data might contribute to network congestion. Perhaps I'm overly cautious about the future of Bitcoin. This inscription was made via Gamma.io, with the cost being approximately $50 USD. This is actually the second inscription I've made myself. The first was minting a Punk Noun using OrdinalBot. For that one, I used an image that was created by bot and had minimal knowledge about the process, but I paid with my Bitcoin nonetheless.

metadata.title: Blind monks examining an elephant
metadata.notes: Caption label from exhibit "Floating World," Images & Literary Sources section: Retrospective of an Early Master, Hanabusa Itchô. This lively and humorous image by influential genre painter Hanabusa Itchô (1652-1724) illustrates the well-known Buddhist parable of blind men examining an elephant. In the parable, a king assigns a group of sightless men to examine an elephant and report a description of the animal. Depending on the part of the elephant explored, each man's report is different one man states that an elephant is shaped like a broom (tail), another that an elephant is shaped like a drum (belly), yet another likens an elephant to a thick rope (trunk), and so on.

metadata.comment: I originally wrote this text in Russian on January 8, 2024. I then translated it into English using ChatGPT 4.0. This text is intended to reassure anyone who finds themselves in a similar situation not to feel embarrassed. Enemas are entirely normal and can be very beneficial for health. There’s no reason to treat them as a taboo subject.

Nosso amor vai além do fim. Pra sempre vamos te sentir. Cada passo que você nos guiou foi mais longe do que sonhamos. Você é nossa versão melhor. Nosso legado de amor, nosso maior valor. Em cada memória, em cada som, você é parte de nós, pra sempre vamos te ter. Você é eterno pra nós. Sua luz nunca se desfaz. Seu coração será nossa voz. Te amamos pra sempre, filho.

metadata.title: Ascend
metadata.description:
'Ascend' (2024) is a 1-of-1 artwork and digital artifact inscribed on the Bitcoin blockchain from the project 'The Wild Within,' a series that brings new life to abandoned buildings from a bygone era.

  Based on a real-world physical space that artists Ryan Koopmans and Alice Wexell traveled to and captured, this piece creates a digital rebirth by combining photography with three-dimensional techniques. 'Ascend' is inscribed on a satoshi mined on March 24, 2021, the same day the first artwork from 'The Wild Within' was minted on Ethereum.

  This is the first artwork ever inscribed on Bitcoin to be auctioned in a live sale at Christie’s, and is the only digital artwork in this auction.

  A physical print of 'Ascend' will be on display at the Christie’s London Gallery prior to the live auction on October 11, 2024, and the winning bidder will receive a framed print of the artwork sized to their preference.

  When viewed on the blockchain, the artwork is alive and dynamic. It automatically transitions between day and night modes at 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. GET daily, synchronized with the Bitcoin clock to reflect the time zone of the abandoned building's location in Georgia.

  The architecture depicted in 'Ascend' is the interior of a crumbling sanatorium in Tskaltubo, Georgia, built between 1952 and 1962. Once a popular health destination, thousands of people visited the town’s sanatoriums annually from the 1940s to the 1990s. After the collapse of the USSR, the buildings were abandoned and fell into disrepair.

  Since the early 1990s, the sanatoriums have been slowly dismantled and stripped of their valuable material, leaving behind empty shells of what were once grandiose classical structures. This abandoned lobby in the Iveria Sanatorium, constructed in Classicism style, provided the perfect environment for the artists to apply their creative touch to 'Ascend.'

  Over the past decade, the artists have explored architectural ruins around the world, photographing buildings that have undergone dramatic transitions.

  Upon returning, they digitally introduce vegetation, modify the structure and lighting, and alter the scenes with the intention of reviving the empty spaces, essentially bringing life back into the rooms.

  The result is 'The Wild Within,' a project that represents a surreal collision between the past and future, natural and manmade, physical and digital, and the real and imaginary.

  'Ascend' aims to depict a surreal representation of the cyclical essence of time, delving into architectural history and its intricate connection with the natural world. The artwork also serves to permanently preserve this imagery on the blockchain.

  Many of the buildings depicted in 'The Wild Within' have been demolished in recent years. This building continues to deteriorate and is being slowly disassembled, further emphasizing the primary theme of the work: the passing of time in a cycle of growth and decay.

metadata.Title: Eternal Tides
metadata.About: Eternal Tides is a generative art project by Phenomena that captures the subtle interplay between natural elements and digital expression. The artwork presents the rhythmic motion of waves reaching the shore, meticulously programmed to reflect the ocean's gentle woven motion and the dynamic flux of the Bitcoin Blockchain.
